name: Single-Leg Standing Calf Raise
summary: A unilateral bodyweight exercise that strengthens the gastrocnemius and soleus by raising the body on the ball of one foot.

setup: Stand upright on one foot, keeping the working knee straight but not locked out.
Bend the opposite knee to keep the non-working foot elevated off the floor.
Lightly place a hand on a wall or stable object for balance if needed.
steps: Press through the ball of the working foot to elevate your heel as high as possible.
Pause for a moment at the peak of the calf contraction.
Lower your heel slowly and with control back down to the starting position.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you press up onto your toes, and inhale as you lower your heel with control.

common_faults.fault: Bouncing at the bottom of the movement
common_faults.correction: Pause briefly at the bottom to eliminate the stretch reflex and force the muscles to contract fully.

common_faults.fault: Rolling onto the outer edge of the foot
common_faults.correction: Focus on driving evenly through the ball of the foot, especially through the first metatarsal and big toe.

common_faults.fault: Bending the working knee to assist the lift
common_faults.correction: Keep the knee extended throughout the set to maximize recruitment of the gastrocnemius.

precautions: Hold onto a sturdy surface for balance if you feel unstable standing on one foot.
